commitResults.messageTitle: Updated AGENTS.md with user setup details
Level-0: renamed chatbot to Echo, added greeting and exit, and updated Java setup instructions.

Level-1: Updated the code to echo commands entered by the user, and exit when the user types the command bye. Likewise, I created two private methods: printGreeting and printMessage for a cleaner code, and added Javadocs for them.
Level-2: Added the ability to store whatever text the user enters and display it back when requested.
Level-3: add mark/unmark commands and a Task class (A-Classes)
A-Coding standard: follow the seedu Java coding standard
Created three subclasses that extend Task class, and fixed Echo.java to show the correct output
A-CodeQuality: extract command dispatch out of main
commitResults.messageBody:
main() greets the user, runs the input loop, dispatches every command,
and prints the farewell. The dispatch chain sits at a lower level of
abstraction than the rest of main -- string slicing and Integer.parseInt
next to calls like printGreeting().

This breaks the Single Level of Abstraction Principle and makes main
harder to read as a summary of what the program does.

Let's move the if/else-if command chain into a private handleCommand
method. main() now reads as: greet, loop over input lines dispatching
each, then say goodbye. Behaviour is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: report invalid input instead of crashing
commitResults.messageBody:
Blank todo/deadline/event descriptions, malformed deadline/event syntax
(missing /by, /from, /to), non-numeric or out-of-range mark/unmark
indices, and unrecognized commands all threw uncaught exceptions
(NumberFormatException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) or silently
produced wrong tasks.

Let's add EchoException and validate each command's arguments before
acting on them, catching EchoException once in main and reporting it as
"OOPS!!! <reason>". A-Exceptions extension: every current command now
has specific, user-facing error messages rather than a generic failure.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-5'
A-Packages: move all classes into the echo package
commitResults.messageBody:
All six classes sit directly under src/main/java with no package,
which the coding standard's "put every class in a package" rule flags
and which the course's A-Packages increment asks to fix.

Let's put Echo, EchoException, Task, Todo, Deadline and Event into a
single package, echo, keeping src/main/java as the source root. Six
classes -- one app class, one exception, a four-class task hierarchy --
don't yet have a natural multi-package split; that becomes worthwhile
once Echo itself is broken into Ui/Parser/Storage/TaskList in a later
increment. Update the README's file path and run instructions to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Level-6: add delete command; store tasks in an ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list is a fixed Task[100], so there's no way to remove a task
and no natural way to shrink the list -- deleting would mean shifting
elements by hand and tracking a separate count that can get out of sync.

Let's replace Task[] + taskCount with a List<Task> (A-Collections
extension) and add a `delete <n>` command that removes the task at that
position and reports the remaining count, reusing the existing
parseTaskNumber validation shared with mark/unmark.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: save tasks to disk and load them on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks only live in memory, so the whole list is lost every time the
chatbot exits -- there's no way to pick up where you left off.

Let's add a Storage class that writes the task list to ./data/echo.txt
(one task per line, pipe-separated, e.g. "D | 0 | return book | June
6th") after every add/mark/unmark, and reads it back into memory at
startup. Each Task subtype knows how to render its own save-file line
via toSaveFormat(), mirroring the existing toString() pattern.

Handle the two required edge cases: a missing file or data/ folder at
startup just yields an empty list (Storage.load short-circuits on
Files.exists, and Storage.save creates the folder before writing), and
a corrupted line is skipped rather than failing the whole load. A save
failure (e.g. disk full) is reported to the user instead of crashing
the running session.

Use java.nio.file.Path for the file path so it stays OS-independent,
and a relative path (data/echo.txt) rather than an absolute one so the
app works regardless of where it's checked out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-6'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
commitResults.messageBody:
branch-Level-6 (ArrayList<Task> + delete) and branch-Level-7 (Storage
save/load against the old Task[]) were developed in parallel from the
same base, so both touched Echo.java's storage and the methods around
add/mark/unmark.

Resolve by keeping the ArrayList from Level-6 and adapting Level-7's
Storage to it: Storage.save(Task[], int) becomes Storage.save(List
<Task>), loadTasks() becomes tasks.addAll(storage.load()), and
deleteTask() now also calls saveTasks() so a delete persists too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP (1/3): extract Ui, make Echo instance-based
commitResults.messageBody:
Echo is one class with ~15 static methods doing everything: reading
input, printing every kind of message, parsing commands, and holding
the task list. There's no separation between "how a result is shown"
and "what the result is".

Let's pull every print/read concern out into a Ui class (showGreeting,
showGoodbye, showError, showTaskList, showTaskAdded/Deleted/
StatusChanged, showMessage, readCommand), matching the course's "Ui:
deals with interactions with the user". Echo now owns a Ui instance
instead of calling static println helpers directly, and becomes an
ordinary object itself -- a constructor that loads from storage, a
run() loop, and main() just does `new Echo(path).run()` -- matching
the target shape in the A-MoreOOP example.

Output is byte-for-byte identical to before this change (diffed a full
command sequence including every message type and an error case
against the pre-refactor build).

TaskList and Parser extraction are separate follow-up commits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP (2/3): extract TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Echo holds a raw List<Task> field directly and calls .add()/.remove()/
.get()/.size() on it from four different methods, so the "this is a
task list with these operations" concept has no name of its own -- it
reads as "a class that happens to have a list field", not as a
collaborator Echo delegates to.

Let's add a TaskList class (the course's "TaskList: contains the task
list, e.g. add/delete operations") wrapping the ArrayList, with add/
remove/get/size plus asList() for the two places (Ui, Storage) that
need a plain List<Task> to display or persist. Echo's method bodies
are otherwise unchanged -- it was already calling tasks.add(...) etc,
so TaskList's method names match on purpose to keep this a pure
extract-class move.

Verified byte-identical output against the pre-refactor build, plus a
restart test (add two tasks, delete one, restart, confirm the file and
in-memory list agree).

Parser extraction is next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP (3/3): extract Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
requireDescription/parseDeadline/parseEvent/parseTaskNumber lived as
private methods on Echo, mixed in with the task-list mutation and
persistence logic they feed into. There was no single place that
answers "how do we make sense of a command line" independent of what
Echo then does with the result.

Let's move those four methods to a new Parser class (the course's
"Parser: deals with making sense of the user command"), unchanged
except parseTaskNumber now takes a taskCount parameter instead of
reading Echo's task list directly -- Parser has no reason to know
about TaskList, it only needs a bound to validate against. Parser's
constructor is private since every method is a stateless static
helper.

Echo.handleCommand keeps the if/else dispatch but each branch now
calls Parser.xxx(...) for the parsing/validation and then acts on the
result itself (add/mark/unmark/delete + save). Echo shrank from 280 to
142 lines across the three A-MoreOOP commits.

Verified byte-identical stdout and save-file contents against the
pre-refactor build on an extended run covering every command, every
validation error, and the unknown-command path, in isolated working
directories.

This completes the Minimal tier of A-MoreOOP: Ui, Storage (already
existed), Parser and TaskList are all separate classes, and Echo is
now the thin orchestrator shown in the course's target example.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP stretch (1/2): turn each command into a Command object
commitResults.messageBody:
Echo.handleCommand still decided what to do for each input with an
if/else chain and then did it through private helpers on Echo
(addTask, deleteTask, markTask, unmarkTask, saveTasks). Adding a new
command meant editing both the dispatch chain and Echo's own methods.

Let's follow the A-MoreOOP stretch goal: an abstract Command with
execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and isExit(), and one subclass per user
command -- AddCommand, DeleteCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand,
ListCommand, ExitCommand. Parser.parse(fullCommand) now returns the
Command to run, so Echo.run() becomes the loop from the course
example: read -> Parser.parse -> execute -> isExit. Echo shrinks to
its constructor, run() and main().

Parser.parse takes only the input line (as in the course example), so
it can no longer check a task number against the list size. The range
check moves into Command.checkTaskNumber, called by Delete/Mark/
Unmark at execute time, with the same error message as before. The
other Parser helpers become private since parse() is now the only
entry point. End of input is parsed as an ExitCommand, which keeps the
old "say goodbye on EOF" behaviour.

Verified against the pre-A-MoreOOP build in isolated directories:
stdout and data/echo.txt are byte-identical for every command, every
validation error, EOF without bye, loading a saved file, and a save
file containing corrupted lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP stretch (2/2): frame each response in run(), as in the example
commitResults.messageBody:
Every Ui.showXxx method drew its own divider lines, so the framing of
a response was decided separately by each message type rather than
once per command. The course's target run() instead draws one line
after reading the command and one in a finally block, so every
response -- normal output or error -- gets exactly one frame.

Let's match that: add Ui.showLine(), have run() call it before
parsing and in finally, and make the per-command Ui methods print
their text without lines (showMessage becomes a private unframed
helper). showGreeting is outside the loop, so it frames itself.

Output is byte-identical to before for every normal command, every
validation error, EOF, loading a saved file and a corrupted save file.
The one visible difference is when writing the save file fails: the
"Could not save your tasks" error now appears inside the same frame
as the command's response instead of in a second frame of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-9: add find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
With a long task list the only way to locate a task is to scroll
through `list` and read every line.

Let's add `find <keyword>`, which prints the tasks whose description
contains the keyword, numbered from 1 in list order, under "Here are
the matching tasks in your list:" (the course's example format).
Matching is a plain case-sensitive substring check; an empty keyword
is rejected with an error, like the other commands' missing-argument
errors.

The pieces follow the existing structure: Parser.parse maps `find` to
a FindCommand, TaskList.find does the filtering, Task.containsKeyword
does the per-task check so the description field stays private, and
Ui.showMatchingTasks prints the result. showTaskList and
showMatchingTasks share one private helper for the numbered list
instead of duplicating the loop.

All earlier regression scenarios (every command, every error, EOF,
loading and corrupted save files) still give byte-identical output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8 (1/2): store deadline dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
A deadline's /by part is kept as free text, so "2019-10-15" is just a
string to the chatbot: it can't be validated, reformatted or compared.

Let's store it as a java.time.LocalDate, as the Level-8 Minimal goal
asks: users type yyyy-mm-dd (e.g. 2019-10-15) and the task shows it
as MMM dd yyyy (e.g. Oct 15 2019). A new Dates class holds the parse
and display logic in one place; the display formatter pins
Locale.ENGLISH so month names stay "Oct" on a machine set to another
language (checked with user.language=ru).

An invalid or impossible date (e.g. "Sunday", "2019-02-30") is
rejected with an error naming the expected format. The save file
stores the date as yyyy-mm-dd. A deadline line whose date can't be
parsed -- e.g. one saved before this change as "June 6th" -- is
treated like any other corrupted line and skipped on load instead of
crashing at startup.

Everything not involving deadline dates behaves exactly as at Level-9
(diffed todo/event/mark/unmark/delete/find, their errors, EOF and
loading a save file against the Level-9 build).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8 (2/2): add `on <date>` command; store event dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
With deadlines now stored as dates, the chatbot still can't answer
"what do I have on a given day?", and events keep their start/end as
free text, so they can't take part in any date comparison.

Let's do the Level-8 stretch goal: a command that prints the
deadlines/events occurring on a specific date. `on 2019-10-15` lists
deadlines due that day and events whose range includes it (start and
end days inclusive), numbered from 1. To make events comparable,
their /from and /to become LocalDate too, typed as yyyy-mm-dd and
shown as e.g. Oct 15 2019, matching deadlines.

Each task decides for itself whether it falls on a date via
Task.isOn (false for plain tasks, overridden by Deadline and Event),
so TaskList.findOn and the new OnCommand need no type checks.

New errors: an event that ends before it starts, an invalid event
date, and `on` without a date or with an invalid one. The deadline
and event "missing part" errors now give yyyy-mm-dd examples. An
event line in the save file whose dates can't be parsed (e.g. saved
before this change as "Mon 2pm") is skipped on load, like a deadline.

Commands without dates (todo, list, mark, unmark, delete, find) and
their errors behave exactly as at Level-9.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: A-JavaDoc: document every remaining class member
commitResults.messageBody:
Every class and every non-overriding public/protected method already
had a header comment, which meets the A-JavaDoc Minimal goal. What was
left undocumented was Echo.main, the @Override methods (each
Command's execute, ExitCommand.isExit, and the toSaveFormat overrides
in Todo/Deadline/Event) and the private no-op constructors of the
static-only Parser and Dates classes.

Let's add header comments to all of those to reach the stretch goal:
every non-private class and method, plus the private methods. The
override comments say what that specific subclass does (e.g. which
save-file line it produces, which error it can throw) rather than
repeating the parent's generic description.

Comment-only change: the javadoc tool with -Xdoclint reports no errors
or warnings, and output and save file are identical to the Level-8
build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
